title: Should you isolate your front delts?
summary: Adds nuance to the common claim that presses are enough for front delts. He argues front raises done correctly are a novel, shoulder-friendly stimulus that can even help prevent shoulder injuries, and that well-developed front delts matter for bodybuilding poses. He does heavy front raises 4x10 plus band burnouts.

claims.claim: Presses will give most people good front delt size and strength, but the claim that you never need to isolate them lacks nuance.

The overuse-injury argument against front delt isolation is backwards: shoulder injuries come from the rotator cuff and AC joint under heavy pressing, not the front delt muscle, so isolation can benefit heavy pressers.
Horizontal presses, and vertical presses with poor form, put a lot of pressure on the rotator cuff and AC joint.
The only real front delt isolation is raises; lateral raises involve the front delt little when done properly and cause impingement when done badly.
Done right, front raises are excellent for the front delt and also hit the other heads; the movement pattern appears nowhere else in training, adding a new hypertrophy stimulus.
The 'you never do that in real life' argument against front raises is poor; you never lie on your back and press in real life either.
Front raise technique: pack shoulders back and down like a press, use a false grip to take out the wrist, no swinging, dead stop, no leg bend; 4 sets of 10.
Front delt isolation isn't required, but for maximal delt development as a bodybuilder the front delt matters more than people think.
Whenever the arm is raised in posing transitions the front delt pops out; in a back double biceps it is what sticks out linking biceps peak, traps and head, so its size changes the pose.
If a lift doesn't agree with you, don't do it; but he can go very heavy on front raises pain-free and finds they help prevent his shoulder injuries by training an otherwise unused plane.
One day a week he does very heavy front raises, 4 sets of 10 pushing the weight, then band burnout reps for the pump.
Whether to isolate front delts is goal-specific, like neck or traps; the idea that presses alone give maximal front delt development is ludicrous to him.
He sees himself as challenging fitness dogma wherever he finds it.
